<description>
This PR defers cfilter-related P2P messages if they ask for information from a new block which has been validated, but compact filters are not yet constructed. This PR is a prerequisite for a bigger change of decoupling index construction from block connection to make block announcement faster.

Fixes: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/29655, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/27085
Related discussion: [1](https://bnoc.xyz/t/request-block-filter-peers-being-disconnected-due-to-invalid-block-requests/101/2)

When a new block arrives, block connection has several steps (described very broadly):

1) block connection to the active chain
2) and then comes indices construction (compact block filters index, txdindex) and also wallet updates

If a light peer sends `getheaders` after the first step has passed, but the second has not, the light peer would
then send `getcfheaders` (or another cfilter request) with the stop hash of the new block. Core has no filters yet and thus doesn't answer, and the light peer thinks Core misbehaves and disconnects.

This race condition is extremely rare right now, because normally headers are received via BIP130 and in that case the light client would not receive a new header until Core is ready to serve the filters (Core does not announce block until the filters are constructed, but can respond with a new header if explicitly asked). So to hit the race condition, the light client has to actively poll the Core node with `getheaders`.

Active polling is not prohibited by BIP157 and in my opinion it should not be (at the very least, light clients need
to sync and have to send `getheaders` with a zero stop hash, which might hit the race). Once Core has sent the block in a `headers` reply, the stop hash "is known to belong to a block accepted by the receiving peer".

This race condition would occur far more frequently (on every new block if light client is fast enough) if new header
announcements were made without waiting for index construction (which we'd love to see in the future). It is discussed here: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35023. In that case light clients would receive new header announcements from Core without the need to actively poll it.

The approach used (via https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35023#issuecomment-4332885607) is to stop processing all messages from a peer if there is a request from it which we cannot answer right now, but will be able to shortly. So this PR introduces a way to stop processing requests from a peer, which later can be used to park a peer who sent us a new block (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35354#issuecomment-5363737198).

What it adds:

A `getcfilters`, `getcfheaders` or `getcfcheckpt` request that is racing the filter index is parked instead of being ignored:

  1. `PeerManagerImpl::ShouldDeferCFilterRequest` checks whether a request is racing the index construction: the index is synced, but has not yet caught up with the tip, and does not cover the requested stop hash yet. It never defers during IBD, where the index can lag the tip for a long time.
  2. If so, the request is stored in the peer's `m_pending_request` and we stop processing further messages from that peer. This keeps responses in order; other peers and outgoing messages are not affected.
  3. The parked request is retried whenever we process that peer's messages, at most once every 100ms (`PARKED_CF_RETRY_INTERVAL`) to avoid taking `cs_main` too often.
  4. If the request is still parked after 5s (`MAX_CF_PARK_INTERVAL`), we stop waiting and serve what we can: the peer gets the answer if the filters exist by then, otherwise the request is ignored, as it was before this PR. The peer then continues to be processed normally.

A new `cfilter_race_tests` suite (`src/test/cfilter_race_tests.cpp`) uses a `PreFilterBlocker` `CValidationInterface` registered before the filter index, so its own `BlockConnected` fires first on the scheduler thread and stalls it before the filter index gets to run `CustomAppend`. This reproduces the race window deterministically. The tests drive the real message processing path via `ConnmanTestMsg` and advance the mocked clock where time matters.

Cases covered:

  - `deferred_cfilter_response_reaches_peer` — a racing `getcfilters` is parked, not answered and not dropped, and is answered once the index catches up.
  - `deferred_cfheaders_response_reaches_peer` — the same for `getcfheaders`.
  - `pending_request_pauses_message_processing` — while a request is parked, a later `ping` from the same peer is not processed, and the responses come back in request order.
  - `parked_request_retries_are_throttled` — a parked request is not retried before the retry interval has passed, even if the filter is ready.
  - `parked_request_is_released_after_timeout` — after the park timeout the peer is no longer paused (a later `ping` is answered), and no filter is sent for a filter that does not exist.

I've used Claude Code for this PR.

P.S. Light clients (kyoto, neutrino) also do cross-polling: they ask for filters from a peer that didn't announce the
block, naturally receive no answer, and might disconnect it. Disconnection due to cross-polling occurs more frequently than those due to active polling and this PR does not address it directly, as it IMO is a mistake by light clients, not Core's one. Still, this PR gives such cross-polled filter requests an additional window to resolve if the asked node is in the process of filter construction.
Related neutrino discussion: https://github.com/lightninglabs/neutrino/issues/338.
</description>

[2026-11-27] c:7222410634 comment by randomlogin:
@mzumsande thanks for your comments, I changed the PR description in favor of a prerequisite step towards more async block validation and block broadcast.

About changing the BIP:

1) Cross-polling is light clients' implementation bug, they have to be sure they ask only a peer who advertised a
block, so they should not cross-poll or do it carefully, not disconnecting a slow peer (and slow peers naturally occur).

      And yes, there are implementations which do cross-polling (for example https://github.com/2140-dev/kyoto, also Neutrino), I've opened an issue there about that.

      This is correctly specified in the BIP (`StopHash MUST be known to belong to a block accepted by the receiving
peer`). So in general it seems we should not address it here or in any other PR.

2) Active polling (light clients do that, both Neutrino and Kyoto).
    It is allowed by the BIP and I don't see a good way to fix it there: I think specifying the way a light peer gets to know about a new block (via listening to headers instead active polling) would go too much into implementation detail and supposes the way headers arrive to the light node. In case there will be another way of obtaining headers, it would need to address it too (but maybe it is okay?).

   If we try to model desired situation in which light clients only listen to headers, this can work with a long-living peer. But if a light client connects to a new peer and sends sendheaders, Core wouldn't know what is light client's tip and fallback to inv with subsequent getheaders from a light peer. In that sense at least some getheaders are inevitable and can trigger the PR's bug (though quite rare to say the least).

Still I thought we could
1. explicitly prohibit naive cross-polling in the BIP.
2. another thought is that we could add zero stop hash to filter-related requests in the same fashion it is done for `getheaders`. Though I am not 100% sure it is safe to do so and it needs some additional brainstorming.

Also I when opened this PR I emailed BIPs authors, but received no response.
